title: Overnight Ops: Quick-Fix Run-Notes (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick reference for overnight on-call — immediate triage steps, short-term mitigations, and notes for the morning owner. Informal, intentionally terse. Update Confluence + proper runbook after stable mitigation.

CURRENT CONTEXT (as of 03/12 03:20 UTC):
- Symptoms: sporadic OOMs on dedicated inference pool dpool-eu-1, correlated with token-cache growth in traces. High p95 latency on text-generation route /v1/generate for a handful of routes.
- Impact: limited to paid-tier dedicated customers on eu-1; hosted API unaffected so far. Auto-fallback configured but some requests hit dedicated pool before fallback triggers.
- Recent change: rolling kernel upgrade landed 03/11 23:50 by infra team (GH ref above). Looks related but unconfirmed.

Quick checklist (first 10m):
1) Confirm alerts: Datadog dashboard -> query "avg:service.redwood.inference.errors{env:prod} by {pool}" and "avg:service.redwood.inference.memory.used{pool} by {host}".
2) Check PagerDuty incident SRE-789 for notes and acknowledgment.
3) Slack: post short status in #ops-urgent and #sre (tag @oncall).
4) Verify fallback policy status in Console -> routing -> eu-1 -> fallback: should be ON. If OFF, enable immediate fallback.

Useful commands (prod access required):
- kubectl (kubecontext: prod-eu-1):
  - kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l pool=dpool-eu-1
  - kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -i OOM
  - kubectl logs <pod> -c inference --since=2h | tail -n 300
- Check service memory/pid: ssh to host and run: ps aux | grep redwood-inference && pmap <pid> | tail -n 20
- Restart quick (soft): kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-inference-dpool-eu-1 -n redwood-serving (note: triggers cold caches)
- Scale down to reduce load: kubectl scale deployment/redwood-inference-dpool-eu-1 --replicas=1 -n redwood-serving (temporary; ensure capacity elsewhere)
- If pod in CrashLoopBackOff and no obvious logs: kubectl exec -it <pod> -c inference -- /bin/sh -c 'ls -la /var/log && tail -n 200 /var/log/inference.log'

Temporary mitigations (fast, reversible):
- Option A: Enable extra fallback routing (preferred): Console -> routing policy for eu-1 -> increase fallback weight to 100% for hosted-variants. This reduces impact quickly and buys time to debug dedicated pool.
- Option B: Evict offending pods: cordon host -> delete pods -> allow k8s to reschedule (risk: bursts during reschedule).
- Option C: Force-restart inference service on host (systemctl restart redwood-inference) only if pod-level restart doesn't help and CPU/memory on host is saturated.

Escalation matrix (who to page):
- First: @oncall-sre (primary) — see PagerDuty SRE-789.
- If root-cause suspected in infra kernel/k8s: page Infra Lead (Ethan Park).
- If model-level regressions suspected (large sequence lengths causing KV blowups): page Applied ML (Leila Soto).

Quick triage notes to leave for morning (fill these before ending shift):
- Time window observed and rough frequency of OOMs (e.g., 02:10–03:05, ~6 events).
- Which hosts/pods restarted and when (pod names + timestamps).
- Exact mitigation taken (fallback enabled / scaling / restarts).
- Any customer pings or SE tickets opened (copy ticket keys).
- Logs snippet: paste 5–10 lines showing the OOM or memory growth pattern.

Known failure mode to watch for: token-cache leak
- Indicator: steady memory climb with long-running requests and large prompt sizes (-> kv-cache not cleared).
- Quick check: grep for "KV cache size" in inference logs; sample log line: "kv_cache.size=... seq_len=..."
- Temporary workaround: set request-size soft-limit via routing policy to 2048 tokens for the pool (Console -> model policies -> token limit). That reduces peak memory usage but may impact customer requests. Notify CS.

Notes / TODOs (follow-up in morning):
- Run heap/profile on one affected pod (ask infra to attach pmap + jmap if JVM; for native runtime gather memory-snapshots).
- Correlate with GH PR infra#2184 (kernel/driver changes) — re-run repro with old kernel in staging.
- Add a persistent monitor on kv_cache.size per pod and alert at 80% of pod mem.
- Draft proper runbook entry (Confluence): permanent mitigations + clear rollback play.

Snippets to paste into Jira/Slack when opening incident:
- "Observed sustained memory growth on dpool-eu-1 leading to OOMs ~02:10–03:05 UTC. Mitigations: enabled fallback to hosted-variants, restarted 3 pods, scaled replicas from 3->1. Investigating token-cache growth and recent kernel upgrade (GH#2184)."

Hand-off template for next shift (copy into their notes):
- What I did: [bullet actions]
- Current state: [healthy | degraded | mitigated-but-unresolved]
- Next steps I recommend: [investigation tasks]
- Links: incident JIRA, logs snippets, dashboards, GH PRs

Random bits / notes to self (scratch):
- If you hit rate-limits in console when toggling fallback, do changes via API: POST /api/v1/routing/pools/eu-1/fallback (token in 1Password).
- Be careful with scale->1 on dpool: if other workloads are pinned to same nodes, cold-start latency will spike. Communicate in #gta-alerts.
- If you tag a customer-facing outage, coordinate message with @CS-ops and use the template in /ops/templates/outage-message.md.

End of doc. Update me in the morning with what you ran. I'll add formal runbook items once root cause nailed down.
